summary: agent-kit's own standards conformance map: each clause, the mechanism, its evidence, its status.

rows.mechanism: policy untrusted-content: content is data, invisible-instruction and override gates; untrusted MCP write/exec denied
rows.why: refused at edit and commit; trust levels deny effects

rows.mechanism: policy secrets -- the one catalogue of secret shapes, its contract published by path for a tree-and-history scanner (the stack-kit adapter's bridge); memory policy refuses secrets in product memory
rows.why: a secret is refused at edit, commit and in memory

rows.mechanism: pinned kit, take by provenance with digests, actions pinned by SHA
rows.why: integrity pinned; authenticity not established until releases are signed (owner's decision)

rows.clause: one source for the pinned kit: no vendored copy beside a submodule
rows.mechanism: referenced install mode: the lock references the kit in the host's tree at a commit; check, the entry point and the served hooks hold it to the lock
rows.why: a referenced host carries one copy of the kit, and an edited, moved or missing one is refused

rows.mechanism: a worker's tree is judged on return before it may enter (admission)
rows.why: no worker output enters the host unjudged

rows.mechanism: route cells: mechanical work never dispatched, task classes, MCP trust, roles as profiles of tools and change scope
rows.why: agency is declared per route and per server

rows.mechanism: briefings carry no secret (secrets policy over every served file)
rows.why: nothing secret is served; leakage of what is served is a product property

rows.mechanism: context budgets per layer, route caps (budget, wall-time stop), spawn ceiling
rows.why: every layer and every run is capped

rows.clause: LLM04 data poisoning, LLM08 embeddings, LLM09 misinformation
rows.mechanism: out of a repository framework's reach: no training, no vector store
rows.why: the kit trains and retrieves nothing

rows.mechanism: edit gates at every write, blocking hooks fail closed, destructive commands get a recovery point
rows.why: a hook that cannot decide refuses

rows.mechanism: memory policy: no secret, no copy of a repository fact; pointer-only
rows.why: memory notes judged on every check

rows.mechanism: results accepted by oracles only; evals judge by gates, never by the worker
rows.why: the eval oracle is the evaluating host's gates

rows.mechanism: doors: one named approval per decision, recorded on every act
rows.why: every act records who decided

rows.mechanism: a message from another agent is never approval (role protocol); dispatch adapters found by contract
rows.why: declared in every role; not machine-enforced across products

rows.clause: Govern, Map, Measure, Manage / AI management system
rows.mechanism: organisational standards: the kit supplies evidence (laws, doors, run records, evals, conformance map) an organisation's system cites
rows.why: a management system is an organisation's, not a repository's

rows.mechanism: contract mcp-servers by trust, served to each product's MCP file
rows.why: stdio and streamable HTTP, names only for secrets

rows.mechanism: task records use A2A states (submitted, working, input-required, completed, failed); artifacts read from declared channels
rows.why: the states and artifacts, not the HTTP transport

rows.mechanism: contract skills, served per product; name and length rules in the schema
rows.why: validated and served

rows.clause: One instruction file read by most agents
rows.mechanism: codex surface serves AGENTS.md; every product's entry carries the same sections
rows.why: one governance block

rows.clause: gen_ai.operation.name, provider, request/response model, usage tokens
rows.mechanism: run records carry gen_ai.* from what each adapter reads out of its product
rows.why: attribute names in run records; no exporter (owner's cut)

rows.mechanism: every declaration is schema-validated by the kit's own validator
rows.why: a subset of the vocabulary (type, enum, const, pattern, min/max, items, required, properties, additionalProperties, oneOf); no $ref

rows.mechanism: kit, capabilities and schema versions; a newer document is refused
rows.why: versions are read, never assumed

rows.mechanism: policy conventional-commits (opt-in): one calibrated message rule (contract message-rules, gate FF-MESSAGE-RULE), applied by verb message from the git adapter's commit-msg hook
rows.why: a host that takes the policy records a change only with a conventional header; an uncalibrated rule is failed by check and never applied

rows.mechanism: CHANGELOG.md upstream
rows.why: kept by hand, not checked

rows.mechanism: docs/decisions ADRs with decisions and rejected alternatives
rows.why: the content of MADR, not its exact headings

rows.mechanism: normative tree: a MUST names its enforcer; contradiction and loosening are refused
rows.why: coherence checked on every check

rows.mechanism: an http MCP server's bearer token is a named variable, served as Authorization: Bearer
rows.why: no token value in any file

rows.mechanism: edit gate no-invisible-instruction-characters
rows.why: refused at edit and commit

rows.mechanism: verb guard + policy recovery-points
rows.why: recovery point before the command

rows.mechanism: POSTURE applied by the entry point; one receipt per invocation
rows.why: fails closed, and leaves a receipt

rows.clause: session-start, stop, subagent ledger, session-end token log
rows.mechanism: pre-write, pre-exec, pre-spawn, commit and push hooks; the product's own session-start (verb session: one context line), stop (verb stop: the continuity capsule's gate, served only with the capsule) and subagent-stop (verb ledger)
rows.why: served for Claude Code from its documented events; Codex's event names are a claim (codex-cli 0.154.0 by inspection) and not served; no session-end token log

rows.clause: change-record coverage over a review range
rows.mechanism: bundle change-records + verb review
rows.why: uncovered paths named, tri-state report

rows.mechanism: git adapter .githooks/pre-push runs check
rows.why: a red check blocks the push

rows.clause: ground ledger: a fact cached with the digests of its paths
rows.mechanism: verb ground; a packet citing a moved ground is refused
rows.why: a stale premise refuses the dispatch

rows.clause: codex thread limits, browser MCP examples
rows.mechanism: MCP servers are declarations a host or bundle adds
rows.why: cost exceeds benefit: a host declares its own

rows.mechanism: this conformance map
rows.why: cost exceeds benefit: the map carries the rows

rows.clause: obligations derived from an object registry
rows.mechanism: bundle execution-graph, gate FF-EXECUTION-GRAPH
rows.why: a unit cannot declare its way out

rows.mechanism: review report: coverage CHECKED|NOT_ASSERTED, runtime conformance and production readiness NOT_ASSERTED; NOT MEASURED statements throughout check
rows.why: what was not checked is never reported as passed

rows.mechanism: contract owners (a host extension point the core seeds), served into a span of the host's .github/CODEOWNERS by the github-actions adapter through the generic `declared` resolver
rows.why: declared once, served in the product's grammar; the file stays the host's

rows.mechanism: a surface `controls` row: `doctor` names it NOT ASSERTED with the exact `gh api` command a person runs; the generated CI refuses whitespace and conflict markers (git diff --check)
rows.why: an external control: setting it needs a person's rights on the hosting service, and the kit neither sets nor reads it

rows.clause: one identical governance block in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md
rows.mechanism: every product's entry is one projection of the same sections
rows.why: one block, never two

rows.mechanism: boundary measured: LF on disk, UTF-8 at every stream, PATHEXT
rows.why: fixed where met (stdin UTF-8, .cmd shims); not a lesson record

rows.clause: claims, observed write arbitration, capsule CAS
rows.mechanism: core claims and arbitration (ADR-022); bundle shared-tree capsule by compare-and-swap
rows.why: a stale write is refused

rows.mechanism: not built
rows.why: cost exceeds benefit (owner's cut)

rows.mechanism: the memory contract, pointer-only
rows.why: cost exceeds benefit (owner's cut)

rows.mechanism: the existing lesson schema and the frontier's script candidates
rows.why: cost exceeds benefit beyond the lesson schema (owner's cut)

rows.clause: subagent ledger: requested vs verified model, tokens
rows.mechanism: dispatch telemetry for dispatched workers; verb ledger on a product's subagent-stop reads the sub-agent's transcript through hands.ledger: gen_ai.request.model vs gen_ai.response.model, usage, a mismatch named
rows.why: both kinds of sub-agent leave a row; the transcript shape is measured on Claude Code 2.1.301

rows.clause: dispatch packet five fields and spawn budget gate
rows.mechanism: verb spawn + policy spawn-packets
rows.why: silent when compliant, refused when not

rows.mechanism: verb doctor
rows.why: a dead chain is named

rows.mechanism: kit-skills (walk-a-door, propose-a-law, take-a-capability), record-a-change, engineering-standards review chapters
rows.why: the procedures a host walks today; audit/rotate/bootstrap are verbs already (check, start)

rows.clause: Change enablement: standard, normal and emergency changes
rows.mechanism: work classes standard / normal / emergency; a standard change pre-approved by its computed class leaves only its commit (ADR-025)
rows.why: the class is computed, the floor is held at commit and in CI, the emergency owes its card

rows.mechanism: an automated floor on every change, doors only where irreversible; FF-WORK-CEREMONY reads lead time per class
rows.why: safety comes from the floor, not the number of approvals; lead time is read, never typed

rows.mechanism: the undo-cost scale (reversible, costly, irreversible); lowering a card's class is the owner's door (reshape --approve)
rows.why: the weight of the path is the cost of undoing it

rows.clause: rigour scaled to the consequence of failure
rows.mechanism: the lightest class whose envelope admits a change's undo cost and breadth; areas raise it (at_least) and owe records (requires)
rows.why: the scaling is aligned; a safety-integrity certification is an external assessor's

rows.mechanism: a card's uncertainty, each domain with the lightest class it may walk; it only raises the class
rows.why: declared at shaping, held by FF-WORK-CLASSES

rows.clause: tailoring the process to the work, recorded
rows.mechanism: the host tailors by areas (undo cost, at_least, requires, max_areas), never by editing the classes; loosening them owes a card
rows.why: the tailoring is a declaration, and loosening it leaves a record

rows.clause: risk identified, assessed and treated in proportion, continuously
rows.mechanism: weigh before the work (--path), on the working change, at commit and on every pushed commit (--each)
rows.why: the change-level treatment is built; an organisation's risk register is its own

rows.mechanism: after between cards: entering the work waits for what it comes after; REGRESSED when finished work stops holding
rows.why: the gate is computed from the cards

rows.clause: an expedite class of service; WIP limits
rows.mechanism: the emergency class with its debt and clock; wip_limit per state
rows.why: expedite is admitted and owed

rows.clause: a claim is as strong as its evidence
rows.mechanism: evidence classes declared with the kinds of proof worth each; a criterion's needs; JUnit/TRX and review records as proofs
rows.why: a weaker reading leaves a criterion unproven

rows.mechanism: a review record by the card's owner or anyone who moved it proves nothing
rows.why: the author does not grade the work

rows.clause: the simplest workflow that works; agentic complexity only where it earns its cost
rows.mechanism: task classes; weighing is a verb, never a model; the skill walk-a-piece-of-work judges only what is not computed
rows.why: zero tokens where a computation exists

rows.standard: Anthropic, Effective Context Engineering for AI Agents (2025)
rows.clause: context is finite; retrieve just in time
rows.mechanism: a lesson reaches the agent when its area is touched; the board and hot surfaces are bounded (ADR-025 decisions 12, 13)
rows.why: the surface does not grow with the project

rows.mechanism: the delivery lifecycle as a declaration, with doors, computed passages and evidence
rows.why: the life-cycle processes are an organisation's; the kit supplies their records

rows.clause: Risk-based testing: test effort proportional to the risk of what changed
rows.mechanism: an area declares what proves it (proved_by); prove weighs what a push carries and runs that, and everything only where the change owes a decision (ADR-025 amendment 4, Cardinal IX)
rows.why: the selection is computed from declared areas, never chosen by an agent

rows.standard: Change-based test selection (Google TAP; Bazel and Nx affected targets)
rows.clause: Run the tests a change can affect; fall back to all of them where the impact cannot be computed
rows.mechanism: proof_for over the published areas, their downstream (feeds) and the pushed refs; an unmapped place, a heavy change or an unreadable range runs everything and says why
rows.why: the impact map is the host's areas, which it already keeps -- no second map to go stale

rows.standard: Lean software development (Poppendieck 2003; Womack and Jones)
rows.mechanism: Cardinal IX: every cost follows the change it serves; a green proof is never repeated on the same bytes; check --brief for agents
rows.why: both directions are defects: heavier than the failure prevented, or lighter than the risk

rows.clause: An appetite set before the work, and a bet a person places
rows.mechanism: a major card owes an appetite and the owner's bet, a door no machine opens
rows.why: the bet is a door; the appetite is measured where its unit can be read and said where it cannot

rows.standard: Site Reliability Engineering (Beyer et al., Google 2016)
rows.clause: An emergency change ships first and owes its postmortem
rows.mechanism: a Work-Class: emergency trailer a person declares; its debt is repaid by a card holding what its computed class owes, within the host's days
rows.why: a stub card no longer repays it (second audit)

rows.clause: Art. 14: effective human oversight -- a person can decide, override and stop
rows.mechanism: doors only a person opens; where the host declares owner_signing, an owner's mark holds only in a commit the owner signed, verified against the trust root as it stood at the parent
rows.why: an obligation of a provider or deployer; the repository supplies the verifiable oversight it can

rows.clause: LLM06 Excessive Agency: high-impact actions need a human approval the agent cannot grant itself
rows.mechanism: owner signing: a mark is introduced by a commit its principal signed; replayed, re-walked and self-vouched marks fail
rows.why: found forgeable twice by independent review, and closed with a test for each way

rows.standard: git SSH signing (gpg.format=ssh) and OpenSSH allowed_signers
rows.clause: A signature verified against a trust root, the bootstrap trusted on first use
rows.mechanism: verb signer (the owner's own act, passphrase asked by the key tool); one trust root shared with capability provenance (ADR-008)
rows.why: the first registration is trusted on first use, as an SSH host key is -- said, not hidden

rows.mechanism: a review by the work's author, or by whoever carried it through a door, proves nothing
rows.why: authorship is separated; the reviewer's own independence (organisational, financial) is not the repository's to prove

rows.clause: CICD-SEC-1 Insufficient flow control: controls enforced on the server, not only on the client
rows.mechanism: client hooks are feedback a person can bypass; CI runs check on the exact pushed commit on a clean runner with no cache (ADR-025 amendment 5)
rows.why: branch protection that requires the CI check is the forge's, set by the owner

rows.clause: MEASURE 2: the AI system's behaviour is evaluated, not assumed
rows.mechanism: verb trial runs agent evals judged by deterministic oracles; the work skill was measured across five task classes (2026-10-17: five of five walked right)
rows.why: one study and the shipped evals; no recurring behavioural suite yet

rows.clause: Documentation built from its sources and tested
rows.mechanism: the verb table and the host blueprint are derived from the verbs and the host layout, and fail a test the moment they differ
rows.why: a hand-kept table drifted once; these cannot
